rulings.Case Title: JAMES BARBOUR ET AL VS. IMO INDUSTRIES LLC ET AL
rulings.Calendar Matter: Notice Of Motion And Motion For Order Granting Preference In Setting Case For Trial, And Extending Discovery Cutoff
rulings.Rulings: On Asbestos Law and Motion / Discovery Calendar for Tuesday, September 1, 2026, Department 502, Line 2. Plaintiff's Motion for Order Granting Preference in Setting Case for Trial, and Extending Discovery Cutoff is GRANTED under C.C.P. section 36(a). No opposition filed. 1. The trial date is December 21, 2026, at 11:15 a.m. in Department 206. a. Last day pursuant to C.C.P. section 36(f) is December 30, 2026. b. The parties shall follow the California Rules of Court, San Francisco Local Rules, and Local Rule 20. 2. The last day for hearing summary judgment/adjudication motions is December 15, 2026. a. Summary judgment/adjudication motions shall be brought on regular notice pursuant to the relevant provisions of the C.C.P., unless the parties stipulate otherwise. b. Before a party files and serves a summary judgment/adjudication motion, it must contact the clerk to make a reservation. c. The Court allows a maximum of four summary judgment/adjudication motions per day to be calendared, unless good cause is found to exceed this number. Contact the clerk to schedule a good cause hearing. 3. Time to respond to written discovery not yet served is shortened to 20 days. a. For written discovery that has already been served, responses are due within 20 days of this hearing or by the date determined by the C.C.P., whichever is earlier. b. Any issue/dispute that requires meet and confer, shall occur in person or via telephone, not by email or letter. 4. Electronic service is considered the equivalent of personal service. 5. The fact discovery cut-off date is December 4, 2026. 6. The expert discovery cut-off date is December 18, 2026. 7. All bankruptcy documents shall be turned over to defendants no later than October 1, 2026. a. If Plaintiff submits documents to bankruptcy trusts after this date, they must notify Defendants no later than five days after submission. b. The fact discovery cut-off does not apply to bankruptcy documents. (Part 1 of 2, the tentative ruling continues in Part 2 of 2)

rulings.Case Title: WAYNE HOEFER VS. 3M COMPANY ET AL
rulings.Calendar Matter: Notice Of Motion To Specially Set A Trial Date Pursuant To C.C.P. 36(A), And(E)
rulings.Rulings: On Asbestos Law and Motion / Discovery Calendar for Tuesday, September 1, 2026, Department 502, Line 4. Plaintiff's Motion for Order Granting Preference in Setting Case for Trial, and Extending Discovery Cutoff is GRANTED under C.C.P. sections 36(a) and (e). Opposition filed by Defendants (1) BWDAC, Inc's and DCo LLC. Joinder filed by Defendants: 1) American Honda Motor CO., Inc; 2) Kawasaki Motors Corp., U.S.A., Inc; 3) Yamaha Motor Corporation, U.S.A; 4) Pneumo Abex LLC; and 5) Jaguar Land Rover North America LLC. Reply filed. Defendants' opposition is meritless. Where a party meets the requisite standard for calendar preference under [Code of Civil Procedure section 36] subdivision (a), preference must be granted. No weighing of interests is involved." (Fox v. Superior Court (2018) 21 Cal.App.5th 529, 535; see also, e.g., Miller v. Superior Court (1990) 221 Cal.App.3d 1200, 1204 [statute "grants a mandatory and absolute right to trial preference"]; Swaithes v. Superior Court (1989) 212 Cal.App.3d 1082, 1085 [trial court "has no power to balance the different interests of opposing litigants in applying the provision"]; Koch-Ash v. Superior Court (1986) 180 Cal.App.3d 689, 694 [section 36(a) "must be deemed to be mandatory and absolute" and "no discretion is left to trial courts.] 1. The trial date is December 21, 2026, at 11:15 a.m. in Department 206. a. Last day pursuant to C.C.P. section 36(f) is December 30, 2026. b. The parties shall follow the California Rules of Court, San Francisco Local Rules, and Local Rule 20. 2. The last day for hearing summary judgment/adjudication motions is December 15, 2026. a. Summary judgment/adjudication motions shall be brought on regular notice pursuant to the relevant provisions of the C.C.P., unless the parties stipulate otherwise. b. Before a party files and serves a summary judgment/adjudication motion, it must contact the clerk to make a reservation. c. The Court allows a maximum of four summary judgment/adjudication motions per day to be calendared, unless good cause is found to exceed this number. Contact the clerk to schedule a good cause hearing. 3. Time to respond to written discovery not yet served is shortened to 20 days. a. For written discovery that has already been served, responses are due within 20 days of this hearing or by the date determined by the C.C.P., whichever is earlier. b. Any issue/dispute that requires meet and confer, shall occur in person or via telephone, not by email or letter. 4. Electronic service is considered the equivalent of personal service. 5. The fact discovery cut-off date is December 4, 2026. 6. The expert discovery cut-off date is December 18, 2026. 7. All bankruptcy documents shall be turned over to defendants no later than October 1, 2026. a. If Plaintiff submits documents to bankruptcy trusts after this date, they must notify Defendants no later than five days after submission. b. The fact discovery cut-off does not apply to bankruptcy documents. (Part 1 of 2, the tentative ruling continues in Part 2 of 2)
